title: PORTS-Pike: Nvidia stands behind OpenAI's rent on a campus that must run Nvidia systems
summary: Nvidia buys SB Energy stock and guarantees the landlord against an OpenAI rent default. Once buildings are ready, OpenAI will pay rent to SB Energy, and the site must deploy only Nvidia reference architecture. No rent, guaranty or system purchase is in effect yet.

legs.description: Prepaid forward for SB Energy Class N stock, funded; a further placement at the IPO is committed

Residual value guaranties to the PORTS building landlords for leases of about 4.25 GW-IT to an OpenAI affiliate; paid only on tenant insolvency or uncured monetary default; not in force until a building is ready for service, the first expected in Nvidia's fiscal 2029
Rent under 17 twenty-year leases of about 8.0 GW-IT, commencing 2028 to 2032; rent total not disclosed
Compensation to Nvidia for the guaranty under a separate letter agreement; amount not disclosed
The premises must exclusively deploy Nvidia reference architecture for at least 20 years; no purchase value disclosed

circularity_note: Closing leg is sourced as a contractual obligation (site exclusivity), not as a dollar amount. A ratio needs OpenAI's or SB Energy's disclosed spending on Nvidia systems for PORTS-Pike; neither side discloses it, so the ratio is not computable. The guaranty is contingent, not paid (no payments to date, ev_30023).
label: analysis

title: OpenAI: Nvidia equity in, Nvidia-based compute contracts out
summary: Nvidia commits equity to OpenAI's funding round, and OpenAI pairs the investment with dedicated Vera Rubin capacity and contracts with clouds that run Nvidia GPUs. CoreWeave, one of those clouds, runs only Nvidia GPUs, so part of the round can return to Nvidia as hardware sales; no amount is disclosed.

legs.description: Investment in OpenAI's 2026 round, disclosed by OpenAI; funded amount and schedule not disclosed
3 GW of dedicated inference and 2 GW of training on Vera Rubin, paired with the investment; no dollar value
OpenAI master services agreement with CoreWeave of March 2025, signed before the 2026 round, up to about this amount through October 2030
legs.amount_label: up to (contract signed March 2025, before the round)

legs.description: All GPUs in CoreWeave's fleet are Nvidia GPUs; Nvidia was 17% of CoreWeave's 2025 supplier purchases, dollar value not stated

circularity_note: Nvidia's side is sourced only from OpenAI (Nvidia does not name the investment). OpenAI's spending on Nvidia hardware is not disclosed in dollars; the Vera Rubin capacity has no value, and Microsoft's Azure contract does not name Nvidia hardware as use of proceeds, so it does not count under spec/05. Ratio not computable. OpenAI's $250 billion Azure contract (ev_120111, 2025-10-29) predates the February 2026 round, so it is no longer drawn as a leg of this loop.
label: analysis

title: Anthropic: Nvidia stock purchase, then Nvidia GPU capacity from Nvidia-backed clouds
summary: Nvidia buys Anthropic stock in the IPO placement, and Anthropic has agreed to spend on Nvidia GPU compute at SpaceX, Nscale and Lambda. SpaceX and Nscale are Nvidia customers or buy Nvidia GPUs; Lambda's purchases are not on file. Nvidia also holds equity in SpaceX, Nscale and Lambda, so money leaves Nvidia once and can return through several paths.

legs.description: 120,481,927 Class N shares bought in the IPO concurrent private placement, closed 2026-11-20
SpaceXAI arrangements for Nvidia GPU compute into 2029, cancellable on 90 days notice after initial periods
Nscale GPU services agreements for Nvidia GPU compute into 2033; Nscale has no binding financing yet
Lambda agreements for Nvidia GPU compute into 2034; the August 2026 agreement is terminable
SpaceXAI deploys Nvidia Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin systems; no value disclosed
Nvidia is Nscale's primary GPU manufacturer, bought through OEMs; no value tied to the Anthropic contract

circularity_note: Nvidia's funded side is sourced (Anthropic 424B4). The return side is sourced only as supplier relationships without dollar values; none of the three clouds discloses Nvidia hardware bought for Anthropic. Ratio not computable. Nvidia's portion of Anthropic's Series G is not disclosed (rel_anthropic_eqc_2025).
label: analysis

title: CoreWeave: shareholder, supplier, renter and buyer of unsold capacity
summary: Nvidia owns CoreWeave stock, is the maker of every GPU in its fleet, rents compute from it and has agreed to buy capacity CoreWeave cannot sell to its own customers. Money flows to CoreWeave as equity and rent and flows back to Nvidia as GPU purchases, whose dollar value CoreWeave does not disclose.

legs.description: 22,935,780 Class A shares at $87.20, January 2026 (earlier holding cost not disclosed)
Payments under the 2023 master services agreement: about $320m to end 2024, $326.3m in 2025, $59.6m in Q1 2026 (sum $705.9m, analysis)
Order to buy CoreWeave's residual unsold capacity through 2032-04-13, initial value of the order form, not a cap; ends after a 90 day insolvency
All GPUs are Nvidia GPUs; Nvidia was 17% of 2025 supplier purchases; dollar value not disclosed

circularity_note: Round trip can be shown side by side only partly: Nvidia's rent paid is sourced ($705.9m in components) but CoreWeave gives Nvidia's share of purchases (17%) without a dollar figure, and its $7.4bn of OEM financing names no OEM (ev_20090). Ratio not computable without CoreWeave's dollar purchases from Nvidia.
label: analysis

title: Nscale: shareholder, noteholder, lease guarantor and customer
summary: Nvidia holds Nscale preferred shares and convertible notes, guarantees its Ward County lease and rents reserved GPU capacity from it. Nscale buys Nvidia GPUs through OEMs to build that capacity, so Nvidia's cash and credit can come back as hardware demand; no amount is disclosed.

legs.description: Series B, SAFE converted to Series C-3, and Series C-4 preferred shares
2028 convertible loan notes subscribed; a further $1.0bn NVIDIA Sale is committed, closing not confirmed
Guarantee of Nscale's Ward County, Texas lease for its first five years, against a $470.0m escrow and warrants
NVIDIA master cloud services agreement for reserved GPU cluster capacity in Iceland, the UK and Norway
Nvidia is the primary manufacturer of Nscale's GPUs, bought through third-party OEMs; no dollar value

circularity_note: Nvidia's side is sourced from Nscale's S-1/A only (Nvidia names neither the stake nor the notes; the guarantee appears anonymously at $860m). Nscale's purchases go through OEMs, which count under spec/05 only where a filing names Nvidia hardware; the S-1/A names Nvidia as primary GPU manufacturer but gives no dollar value. Ratio not computable.
label: analysis

title: IREN: Nvidia cloud contract and share rights booked into GPU cost
summary: Nvidia signed a five-year cloud services contract with IREN and received a right to buy IREN shares. IREN buys GPUs from Nvidia and booked the value of Nvidia's share rights as part of the cost of those GPUs, so part of the GPU price is paid in IREN equity options.

legs.description: Five-year cloud services contract under which Nvidia is IREN's customer
Right for Nvidia to buy up to 30 million IREN shares at $70, vesting with delivery of up to 600,000 GPUs; not exercised as reported
GPUs acquired from Nvidia; the rights' fair value of about $793.4m was capitalised into their cost (dollar value of the GPU purchase not stated)

circularity_note: Nvidia's payments under the contract are not disclosed (only total contract value). IREN's GPU purchases from Nvidia have no stated dollar total; the $793.4m fair value is a component of cost, not the purchase price. Ratio not computable; a round trip needs IREN's disclosed Nvidia purchases and Nvidia's payments in the same window.
label: analysis

title: NAVER: Nvidia equity tied to a Brookfield GPU vehicle that NAVER guarantees
summary: Nvidia's investment in NAVER was conditional on NAVER securing project financing, which it met with a Brookfield vehicle that will buy GPUs and data centers. NAVER guarantees its cloud unit's usage fees to the vehicle, and the expansion is an Nvidia DSX AI factory, so Nvidia's equity helps trigger financing that buys Nvidia systems.

legs.description: Private placement of new NAVER shares; precondition met 2026-10-27, closing pending
Brookfield vehicle to invest in GPUs and data centers and provide computing power to NAVER Cloud; GPU vendor not named in the NAVER release
legs.amount_label: up to (vehicle investment; vendor not named)

legs.description: NAVER guarantees NAVER Cloud's usage fees to the vehicle for up to eight years
Nvidia is a strategic limited partner in Brookfield's AI infrastructure fund; amount not disclosed; link to the NAVER vehicle not stated

circularity_note: Open at the closing leg: the Nvidia release describes the site as an Nvidia DSX AI factory, but no allowed source states that the Brookfield vehicle's GPUs are bought from Nvidia or their value. Needs the vehicle's purchase terms. Nvidia's $1bn is not yet funded.
label: analysis

title: SharonAI: Nvidia minimum revenue on capacity SharonAI buys Nvidia hardware to build
summary: Nvidia agreed to pay SharonAI minimum revenue for reserved capacity it uses only when third parties do not buy it, with a revenue share. SharonAI committed to buy computing hardware for that capacity, so Nvidia's promise supports demand for its own GPUs.

legs.description: Master Cloud Services Agreement: minimum revenue subject to third-party utilisation; the 8-K says up to $4.88bn, the 10-Q says no fixed aggregate value
Commitment of about $4 billion for hardware and infrastructure in connection with the Nvidia agreement; Nvidia GPUs named in the collateral note, vendor split not stated

circularity_note: Both sides are sourced only by SharonAI. Nvidia's committed amount and payments are not disclosed (headline only). The hardware commitment is about $4bn but the share paid to Nvidia is not stated, so the ratio is not computable. SharonAI says it must keep access to additional financing (ev_80010).
label: analysis

title: Firmus: Nvidia equity and credit support for an Nvidia-only campus
summary: Nvidia is named in three Firmus equity rounds, one of them subject to closing, and gives the Batam campus revenue-sharing and credit support. The campus is a dedicated Nvidia DSX AI factory, so Nvidia's equity and support can return as system sales; no amount is disclosed.

legs.description: Participation in the USD505m round (subject to closing) and follow-on in the USD2bn round; Nvidia amounts not disclosed
Revenue-sharing and credit-support model for the Batam campus through 2034; size, form and trigger not disclosed
Dedicated 360 MW Nvidia DSX AI factory campus, up to 170,000 accelerators; no value

circularity_note: No dollar amount on either side is disclosed. Needs Nvidia's investment amounts and Firmus's purchases from Nvidia. One news report, unconfirmed, says Firmus withdrew its listing application (ev_110048).
label: analysis

title: Nebius: Nvidia warrant money in, sole-supplier GPU purchases back
summary: Nvidia paid for a pre-funded warrant over Nebius shares, and Nebius says it relies on Nvidia for the GPU chips it uses. The loop closes through hardware purchases, but no Nvidia rental, backstop or guarantee was found.

legs.description: Pre-funded warrant over 21,065,936 Class A shares
Nebius relies on Nvidia for the GPU chips it uses; purchase value not disclosed

circularity_note: Nvidia's side is reconciled on both sides. Nebius does not disclose its Nvidia purchases, so the ratio is not computable.
label: analysis

title: SpaceX: Nvidia holds SpaceX shares partly from xAI stakes, and SpaceX buys Nvidia systems
summary: Nvidia holds SpaceX shares that came at least partly from xAI stakes when SpaceX acquired xAI; their cost is not disclosed. SpaceX's AI unit is an Nvidia customer, finances its GPUs through lessors with no Nvidia money found, and sells the capacity to Anthropic, another Nvidia investee.

legs.description: SpaceX Class A shares held by Nvidia, at least partly from xAI holdings including the Series E; cost not disclosed
legs.amount_label: cost not disclosed; 13F value $19.7 billion at 2026-09-30

legs.description: Valor leases computing equipment to xAI subsidiaries; recorded by SpaceX as failed sale-leaseback debt
Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25bn per month through May 2029 for about 325,000 Nvidia GPUs at Colossus
SpaceXAI deploys Nvidia Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin systems; no value

circularity_note: Nvidia's money in is not sourced as a cost (only market value). SpaceX's Nvidia purchases have no value. Seed A3's Nvidia stake in a GPU vehicle is unconfirmed (single Bloomberg report). Ratio not computable.
